extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institutions (administrators), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel implementing Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX compliance for postsecondary institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance for final Title IX regulations focused on confidential employees, public awareness events, and Title IX Coordinator duties at postsecondary institutions. Covers what institutions and coordinators must do when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination or sex-based harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee disclosure requirements (§106.44(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain their status as confidential for purposes of this part, including the circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator, and must provide information sufficient to enable a student to report to the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final §106.44(d)(2) was revised to require confidential employees to explain their confidential status and the circumstances when they are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator (§106.44(d)(2)(i)), how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and make a complaint of sex discrimination (§106.44(d)(2)(ii)), and that the Title IX Coordinator may offer/coordinate supportive measures or initiate informal resolution or an investigation (§106.44(d)(2)(iii)). These requirements apply to all three categories of confidential employees. The Department declined to require researchers who qualify as confidential employees to include this information in informed consent documents, to avoid interfering with research independence, though nothing prohibits researchers from doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees and supportive measures (§106.44(d)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees must explain that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures; confidential employees themselves may also offer, provide, or coordinate supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added §106.44(d)(2)(iii) to require confidential employees to explain the Title IX Coordinator's ability to offer and coordinate supportive measures. Nothing in the regulations prohibits confidential employees (e.g., a mental health counselor) from providing additional information about supportive measures or being involved in implementing them. However, the Title IX Coordinator must be required to offer and coordinate supportive measures under §106.44(f)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of records provided to confidential employees from investigations (§106.45(b)(7)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence or records provided to a confidential employee must be excluded from an investigation unless the person to whom the confidentiality is owed has voluntarily waived that confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised proposed §106.45(b)(7)(i) to protect information shared with confidential employees from being used in investigations without the disclosing person's consent. This prevents recipients from being required to gather records or interview confidential employees during investigations and is intended to preserve trust in confidential resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on appointing confidential employees as appointed advisors in live hearings (§106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must not appoint a current confidential employee or an individual who received information as a confidential employee to serve as the advisor appointed to ask questions on behalf of a party during a live hearing in instances where the institution is required to appoint such an advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential employees are not required to act as advisors; while a party may choose a confidential employee as their advisor of choice under §106.46(e)(2), institutions may not appoint (or require) a confidential employee to serve as the appointed advisor in live hearings. This protects legal privileges, avoids conflicts of interest, and respects parties' autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees not required to act as advisors during grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not require confidential employees to serve as advisors in the grievance procedures; they may serve only if chosen by the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves confidentiality protections and prevents requirement-based conflicts with legal privileges. It also responds to commenters' concerns that mandatory advisor roles for confidential employees could negatively impact privileges and trust in confidential resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness event exception scope (§106.44(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The public awareness event exception applies only to a public awareness event held on a postsecondary institution's campus or through an online platform sponsored by the postsecondary institution to raise awareness about sex-based harassment, and covers disclosures of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department limited the exception to on-campus or institution-sponsored online events that raise awareness about sex-based harassment (e.g., Take Back the Night). The exception does not cover off-campus community events, academic assignments, social media posts, or other settings. The Department declined to define 'public event' further, removed language implying additional limits, and clarified that Title IX Coordinators and employees are not required to attend such events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for information disclosed at public awareness events
rubrics_metrics.description: Information disclosed at a covered public awareness event is excepted from certain required actions but still must be reported to the Title IX Coordinator and used to inform the recipient's prevention efforts; the exception does not apply if the information indicates an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant, any students, employees, or other persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to allow institutions to exempt such information from employee notification requirements; such information must be reported to the Title IX Coordinator, who must then determine (via fact‑specific analysis under §106.44(f)(1)(v)) whether the information indicates an imminent and serious threat requiring further action (including whether to initiate a complaint under the grievance procedures). The Department removed automatic cross-references to §§106.45 and 106.46 to avoid implying an automatic initiation of grievance procedures without fact-specific analysis. Institutions must still use the disclosed information to inform prevention efforts (e.g., safety improvements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent 'reasonably may constitute' threshold across provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised wording to refer to conduct that 'reasonably may constitute' sex discrimination or sex-based harassment to align with parallel references throughout the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final edits changed 'may constitute' to 'reasonably may constitute' in several provisions (e.g., §106.44(d)(2), §106.44(e)) to improve consistency and align with §106.44(c). This threshold governs when recipients and Title IX Coordinators must respond under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibilities and required actions (§106.44(f)(1)(i)-(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the recipient's compliance with Title IX and, upon being notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, must take the actions set out in §106.44(f)(1)(i)-(vii) to promptly and effectively end any sex discrimination in the recipient's education program or activity, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the recipient remains ultimately responsible for compliance, §106.44(f) requires Title IX Coordinators to oversee early intervention in response to possible sex discrimination; ensure consistent, equitable treatment of complainants and respondents; provide and coordinate supportive measures; offer resources to end discrimination and prevent recurrence; and respond to patterns, trends, and risk factors. The Coordinator is not required to take the specified actions only if they reasonably determine the alleged conduct could not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and multiple-designation flexibility for Title IX Coordinator duties (§106.8(a) and §106.44(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may designate more than one employee to serve as Title IX Coordinator and may delegate specific duties of the Title IX Coordinator to one or more designees, or permit a Title IX Coordinator to delegate duties, but the Title IX Coordinator must retain ultimate oversight for offering and coordinating supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations permit flexibility and discretion in how duties are assigned and delegated within an institution. This preserves institutional options while ensuring centralized oversight and accountability for core Title IX functions, including offering and coordinating supportive measures.
